input.explanation:
Fault: `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases made this month without checking that the count is non-zero. Any account with no purchases in the current month (a brand-new shopper, or anyone who hasn't bought yet this month) makes `len(bought) == 0` and the function raises ZeroDivisionError, which surfaced as the account-page 500s.

Turning `legacy-checkout-fallback` off did not create the bug; it merely routed account-page traffic into this code path. Since roughly 30% of account requests are for shoppers with no purchases this month, the error rate tracked the rollout fraction exactly (9% at 32/200 off, 31.5% fully off). Flipping the flag back on only hid it.

Fix: guard the divisor. With no purchases this month the average spend per item is defined as 0 cents, which is the correct, representable answer rather than an exception. Also completed `Account.__init__`, which stored only `purchases` and left `total_cents`/`total_this_month_cents` unset — every read of `account.total_this_month_cents` would have raised AttributeError, so the summary path could not have worked at all for any account.

Tests cover both the shopper who bought (average is computed correctly, floor division as before) and the shopper who bought nothing this month (returns 0 rather than raising), plus an account with purchases only in previous months.
input.summary: Return 0 instead of dividing by zero when an account has no purchases in the current month
